chunks.summary: The course covers digital systems from binary fundamentals through Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits, up to a basic ALU/control unit and hardware description languages.
chunks.text: This is the syllabus/orientation deck for 'Digital System Fundamentals' (พื้นฐานระบบดิจิตอล) with its companion lab course 'Digital System Fundamentals In Practice' (ปฏิบัติการพื้นฐานระบบดิจิตอล). The course description states the topic sequence: Introduction to Digital Systems; Binary Systems; Boolean Algebra and Simplification; Combinational Circuits; Sequential Components (latches, flip-flops, registers, counters); Sequential Circuits; a Basic ALU (Arithmetic and Logic Unit) and Control Unit; and Hardware Description Language (HDL). This same order is followed by the Tocci textbook chapters used in this corpus: Ch.1 (intro concepts), Ch.2 (number systems/codes), Ch.3 (describing logic circuits/Boolean algebra), Ch.4+ (combinational logic), and later chapters on flip-flops, counters, and HDL-based design leading into the lab's top-down FPGA design flow (Lab 6, Lab 7).

chunks.summary: Teaching combines lecture, child-centered/time-constrained activity, and assignments; theory is graded final-exam-heavy while lab is graded on punctuality, lab submission, and a lab exam.
chunks.text: Teaching and learning activities (กิจกรรมการเรียนการสอนและวิธีสอน) consist of: classroom lecture (การบรรยายในห้องเรียน), a child-centered approach constrained by time (Child center + Time constrain), and assignments. Theory evaluation (การประเมินผลทฤษฎี) is: final exam 75%, and an optional project/piece of work (ชิ้นงาน) 25%, totaling 100%. Lab evaluation (การประเมินผลปฏิบัติ) is: arriving to lab on time 20%, submitting lab work 50%, and a lab exam 30%, totaling 100%. This means lab performance is graded primarily on deliverables (lab reports/submissions) rather than a single exam, unlike the theory course which is exam-weighted.

chunks.summary: The reference textbook is Tocci/Widmer/Moss 'Digital Systems: Principles and Applications' (Pearson); a QR code is provided as the main communication channel for course announcements.
chunks.text: The prescribed textbook (ตำราเรียน) is 'Digital Systems: Principles and Applications', published by Pearson Education, Inc. — this is the Tocci, Widmer, and Moss textbook (11th edition) whose slide decks form the basis of Chapters 1-12 in this course's content corpus. The main communication channel (ช่องทางหลัก) for the course is given as a QR code (likely linking to a LINE group, Google Classroom, or similar platform) rather than plain text, so students are expected to scan it during orientation to join the course's official channel.
chunks.figure_note: Page 10 states the textbook title 'Digital Systems: Principles and Applications, Pearson Education, Inc.' (the Tocci/Widmer/Moss textbook). Page 11 shows a QR code under the heading 'ช่องทางหลัก' (main channel) for students to scan and join the course's communication channel; the QR's destination cannot be read from the image alone.

chunks.topic: Lab Partners and FPGA Board Hardware
chunks.summary: Labs are done in pairs, one group per section, each pair issued one old FPGA board and one new FPGA board so students learn both platforms.
chunks.text: Lab partnering rules: one group is formed 'from each sec' (section), with 2 people per group, and each group receives 1 New FPGA board and 1 Old FPGA board. The slide shows photographs of both boards: the 'Old board' is a green PCB labeled 'FPGA SERVEYOR-6 XC6SLX9' (a Xilinx Spartan-6 XC6SLX9-based board) made by Apex Instrument Co., Ltd., featuring a DIP switch bank, push-buttons (PB1-PB6), slide switches (SW0-SW7), LEDs, and 4-digit seven-segment displays, with ribbon-cable headers for expansion. The 'New board' is a white PCB labeled 'SPARTAN 7 ...EDGE' (a Xilinx/AMD Spartan-7 based board), which additionally integrates a camera module (OV-series), a small TFT/LCD display, push-buttons, slide switches, seven-segment displays, a buzzer, USB and VGA/DB9 connectors, and what appears to be a Bluetooth/RF module — a substantially more capable I/O set than the old board. This matches the project's target device family (Spartan-7 XC7S15) noted in the ecosystem's architecture decisions.
chunks.figure_note: Page 12 shows side-by-side photos: left is the 'Old board' (green PCB, Xilinx Spartan-6 XC6SLX9, DIP switches, push-buttons PB1-PB6, slide switches SW0-SW7, LEDs, 4-digit 7-segment display, ribbon headers, labeled 'FPGA SERVEYOR-6 XC6SLX9' by Apex Instrument Co., Ltd.); right is the 'New board' (white PCB, Xilinx Spartan-7, with a camera module, small color LCD, push-buttons, slide switches, 7-segment display, buzzer, USB, VGA/DB9 connector, and an RF/Bluetooth module).

chunks.summary: Labs 6 and 7 introduce top-down digital design methodology, which the course allows to be done either by hand or by computer (i.e., HDL/tool-assisted).
chunks.text: The final orientation slide previews Labs 6 and 7 as covering 'Top-Down Design', explicitly noting the design work in these labs can be done 'By Hand or By Computer'. This foreshadows the later shift in the course from manual gate-level/Boolean design (Ch.3-Ch.7 style) to HDL- and tool-based design flows (VHDL/AHDL, schematic capture, or synthesis tools), which is consistent with the course description's final topics of Hardware Description Language and the ecosystem's own AI-driven, engine-agnostic drawing/synthesis pipeline for the Spartan-7 target.
